method: Direct original-resolution visual assessment against the persisted judge rubric; no candidate prompt was considered.

cases.expected_relation: Identical images must have zero observable loss in every component when the source-role image is also identical.
evidence: The compared image bytes and visible pixels are the same.
All observable rendering, style, content, and technical attributes coincide.

cases.expected_relation: An image compared to itself in the source-fidelity role must have zero source-fidelity and technical loss.
evidence: The source and candidate are the same saved image.
The rubric's source-fidelity and technical observations therefore have no mismatch.

cases.expected_relation: The untouched photographic source preserves source content but visibly fails the teacher's reusable illustrated poster style.
evidence: The candidate is an unstyled casual photograph, not a cel-shaded editorial illustration with print-separated color.
It lacks the target's constrained graphic palette, ink contours, abstract support shapes, paper/overprint treatment, and editorial hierarchy.
Because it is the source image itself, depicted source content is fully preserved.

cases.expected_relation: Swapping display order must not change the cross-domain style losses or the self source-fidelity result when labels retain their semantic roles.
evidence: Role labels, rather than display position, identify style truth, source truth, and candidate.
The observable mismatch remains the photographic candidate's absence of the transferable illustrated poster language.

pass_criteria: Both self-match checks return zero in every reported component.
The cross-domain check has high style losses while retaining zero source-fidelity loss.
The order-swap result equals the labeled cross-domain result.
